requirements.requirement: node2 inventory app log messages are forwarded to a centralized log collector on node1
requirements.summary: inventory.service on node2 logs via syslog tag 'inventory' (cmd-29701ef1e9024d29). rsyslog on node2 forwards programname=inventory messages via TCP omfwd with a disk-assisted queue to node1:601 (cmd-b28f4d2e9f884e31). node1 runs an imtcp listener on 601 (cmd-bf993b28302543ca), firewall opened (cmd-7a82217bef5c4f6b), and forwarded messages were directly observed arriving (cmd-9ee0035bfc364b78, cmd-572a5e93ff5546ab), with no SELinux AVC denials.

requirements.requirement: received messages are persisted on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log
requirements.summary: Directory /var/log/inventory created with correct var_log_t SELinux context (cmd-9408f8db68974067); rsyslog rule writes matched messages to that exact file via a dynaFile template (cmd-bf993b28302543ca); file content directly confirmed containing forwarded inventory log lines from node2 (cmd-572a5e93ff5546ab).

requirements.requirement: log flow keeps working after either system (node1 or node2) restarts
requirements.summary: Healthy baselines captured pre-restart on both nodes (cmd-1f82d3c339f74c40, cmd-74e1667ab33b4f3f). node2 was rebooted (cmd-378ed650f36443ca), a new boot_id was observed (cmd-0ef58ec42ad24d53), rsyslog/inventory services returned active (cmd-aadb13ff536a4611), new log entries were generated (cmd-e5b5a95d503746e9) and confirmed arriving at node1's collector file (cmd-459dbf8eba0949d3). node1 was then rebooted (cmd-88d5c35ac27e42ce), a new boot_id was observed (cmd-2c32a0956d6e490f), rsyslog/listener/firewall rule and prior collected data were confirmed intact (cmd-afc282e320454689), and new forwarded entries continued arriving afterward (cmd-faf61c10a8244d95). This is a full pre-restart/restart/post-restart transition for both nodes, directly demonstrating recovered log flow.

overall_summary: The executor built a working end-to-end centralized logging pipeline: node2's inventory.service emits syslog messages tagged 'inventory', rsyslog on node2 forwards those (TCP, disk-assisted queue) to an imtcp listener on node1:601, and node1 writes them to /var/log/inventory/node2.log with correct SELinux context and firewall access. All three material outcomes - forwarding, correct persistence path, and continued log flow after restarts of both node2 and node1 - are directly demonstrated with pre/post-restart evidence including new boot IDs, recovered services, and new log entries observed reaching the collector file after each reboot. Hygiene is high; the only mutation without a clean final purpose was a quickly-superseded draft of the inventory app script.
limitations: Only sequential single-node restarts were performed (node2 then node1), not simultaneous dual-node restarts; the task's 'after either system restarts' wording is reasonably covered by this but a simultaneous scenario was not tested.

The demo inventory application was created by the executor as a stand-in log source since no pre-existing 'inventory' application was found on node2; this is a reasonable interpretation of an underspecified task input, not a deviation from instructions.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace. Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to a material outcome (app/service creation, rsyslog collector/forwarder config, SELinux context, firewall port, restart evidence gathering). One minor redundant mutation: cmd-8308f0f1c0114396 wrote an initial version of /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh (containing a shell bug with an unused RANDOM_SEED assignment) which was immediately superseded moments later by the corrected script and service creation in cmd-29701ef1e9024d29 - low-risk, fully overwritten, no residue. Post-executor lifecycle snapshots show no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets beyond the intended 601/tcp, and only expected reboot-related temp file churn on both nodes, indicating no abandoned or conflicting state.
